title: This Bridge Hangs From 80,000 Miles of Wire
sources: Golden Gate Bridge Highway & Transportation District 'Design & Construction Stats' + exhibit 'Cross-section of a Main Cable' / Make Tech Easier 'Golden Gate Bridge main cables' / Space Group '27,572 Steel Wires per Cable': each main cable holds 27,572 wires (61 strands), both cables together about 80,000 miles of galvanized steel wire, cable diameter 36 3/8 in (about a yard), wire about 0.192 in (thinner than a pencil)

Golden Gate Bridge exhibit 'Spinning the Main Cables' / PBS American Experience 'Spinning the Cables' / NEH 'Steel into Gold': the cables were spun in place, spinning wheels carrying the wire back and forth over the towers between the anchorages, then compacted into round cables

Encyclopaedia Britannica 'Suspension bridge' / MadeHow 'Suspension Bridge' / Encyclopedia.com 'Suspension Bridge': towers are built first, the cable ends are held by massive concrete anchorages on land, the deck hangs from vertical suspenders; the cables are in tension and the towers carry the load down in compression

Golden Gate Bridge exhibit 'Hanging the Roadway Deck' / HMdb 'Hanging the Roadway Deck' marker: the roadway steel was hung out from the towers in both directions at once so the load on the cables stayed balanced
Britannica 'Suspension bridge': the longest bridge spans in the world are suspension bridges

lines.text: This bridge hangs from eighty thousand miles of wire.
lines.caps: This bridge hangs | from 80,000 miles | of wire.

lines.text: If you need a road over deep, rough water, you can't just stand it on posts.
lines.caps: If you need a road | over deep, rough water, | you can't just | stand it on posts.

lines.text: So you build two giant towers, one near each shore.
lines.caps: So you build | two giant towers, | one near each shore.

lines.text: But a cable pulled tight between them would just drag the towers over.
lines.caps: But a cable pulled tight | between them | would just drag | the towers over.

lines.text: So you tie each end into a huge block of concrete on land, called an anchorage.
lines.caps: So you tie each end | into a huge block | of concrete on land, | called an anchorage.

lines.text: But no single rope is strong enough to hold up a whole road.
lines.caps: But no single rope | is strong enough | to hold up a whole road.

lines.text: So you spin the cable right in the sky, with wheels pulling wire after wire across.
lines.caps: So you spin the cable | right in the sky, | with wheels pulling | wire after wire across.

lines.text: Twenty-seven thousand, five hundred seventy-two wires, each thinner than a pencil, squeezed into one cable a yard thick.
lines.caps: 27,572 wires, | each thinner than a pencil, | squeezed into one cable | a yard thick.

lines.text: Then you hang steel ropes straight down from it, called suspenders.
lines.caps: Then you hang steel ropes | straight down from it, | called suspenders.

lines.text: And you lift the road up in pieces, out from both towers at once, so the cables pull evenly.
lines.caps: And you lift the road | up in pieces, | out from both towers at once, | so the cables pull evenly.

lines.text: You see, the road isn't held up from below. It hangs, and the towers just push straight down.
lines.caps: You see, the road | isn't held up from below. | It hangs, | and the towers just | push straight down.

lines.text: That's why the longest bridge spans on Earth all hang from wire.
lines.caps: That's why the longest | bridge spans on Earth | all hang from wire.
